answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 213 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The tide graph is validated at intake and the voyage frontier is published, as a result the ancestry of every answer is public, and bridge anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Honest users pay that once, farms 38 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
